newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya opposition leader says Moi agrees to meet.
newsitem.headline: Kenya opposition leader says Moi agrees to meet.

text.p: Opposition leader in parliament Michael Wamalwa met Kenya's President Daniel arap Moi on Wednesday and said the Kenyan leader agreed to meet opposition leaders next week.
Wamalwa told a news conference that in 10 minutes of "cordial" talks with him, the president agreed to his request for a meeting between the Kenyan government and opposition leaders next week.

"The president acceded to my request for a meeting between the government and a team of opposition leaders next week. I have immediately initiated consultations with my colleagues in the opposition towards this end," said Wamlawa.
In a bid to defuse pressure for reforms in Kenya, Moi on Tuesday met religious leaders and agreed on the need for a review of the constitution. But no date was set for the review.

But Reverend Timothy Njoya, a leader of the campaign for constitutional reforms before presidential and parliamentary elections this year, dismissed Moi's talks with Kenyan religious leaders as a move that would not sidetrack the reform drive.

Njoya, whose arm was broken by police during July 7 clashes in Nairobi between police and pro-reform protesters, said the opposition-backed National Convention Executive Committee (NCEC) heading the reform drive should have been invited for talks.
